sentences.text: Aaron Burr Jr. -LRB- February 6 , 1756September 14 , 1836 -RRB- was an American politician .

He was the third Vice President of the United States -LRB- 1801 -- 1805 -RRB- , serving during Thomas Jefferson 's first term .	Thomas Jefferson	Thomas Jefferson	Vice President of the United States	Vice President of the United States

Burr served as a Continental Army officer in the Revolutionary War , after which he became a successful lawyer and politician .	Continental Army	Continental Army	Revolutionary War	American Revolutionary War

He was elected twice to the New York State Assembly -LRB- 1784 -- 1785 , 1798 -- 1799 -RRB- , was appointed New York State Attorney General -LRB- 1789 -- 1791 -RRB- , was chosen as a U.S. senator -LRB- 1791 -- 1797 -RRB- , from the State of New York , and reached the apex of his career as vice president .	New York	New York (state)	New York State Assembly	New York State Assembly	New York State Attorney General	New York State Attorney General	U.S. senator	United States Senator	State of New York	State of New York

The highlight of Burr 's tenure as president of the Senate , one of his few official duties as vice president , was the Senate 's first impeachment trial , that of Supreme Court justice Samuel Chase .	impeachment	Impeachment in the United States	Supreme Court	Supreme Court of the United States	Samuel Chase	Samuel Chase

In 1804 , the last full year of his single term as vice president , Burr killed his political rival Alexander Hamilton in a famous duel .	Alexander Hamilton	Alexander Hamilton	famous duel	Burr–Hamilton duel
Burr was never tried for the illegal duel , and all charges against him were eventually dropped , but Hamilton 's death ended Burr 's political career .
After leaving Washington , Burr traveled west seeking new opportunities , both economic and political .	Washington	Washington, D.C.
His activities eventually led to his arrest on charges of treason in 1807 .	charges of treason	Burr conspiracy
The subsequent trial resulted in acquittal , but Burr 's western schemes left him with large debts and few influential friends .
In a final quest for grand opportunities , he left the United States for Europe .
He remained overseas until 1812 , when he returned to the United States to practice law in New York City .	New York	New York (state)
There he spent the rest of his life in relative obscurity .
